Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Some bots misbehave: they flood rooms, or their webhooks keep failing.

> As an administrator, I want misbehaving bots to be stopped automatically,
> and I want to decide when they come back.

Flooding:

- A bot may post at most 10 messages in any 10 seconds. Messages posted through the API and webhook replies both count.
- The message that goes over the limit is rejected and starts a 30-second cooldown. During the cooldown, the posting endpoint responds with `429 Too Many Requests` and a `Retry-After` header (seconds left), and webhook replies are not posted.
- Five more attempts to post during the same cooldown suspend the bot.

Failing webhooks:

- A failed delivery is any response other than `2xx`, a timeout, or a connection error.
- Ten failed deliveries in a row suspend the bot. A successful delivery resets the count.

A suspended bot:

- gets `403 Forbidden` from the posting endpoint;
- receives no webhooks;
- keeps its rooms and messages, and still counts towards its owner's bot limit;
- stays listed on the bots page and shows as "Suspended", with the reason.

Only administrators can reactivate a suspended bot, from the bots page: a "Reactivate" button that asks for confirmation. The limits above are fixed in code; they have no settings.

# Chat Bots Design Notes

## Data Model
- Bots are modeled on `User` with `role: :bot` (in `User::Role`: `enum :role, %i[ member administrator bot ]`) and `User::Bot` concern.
- `users.bot_token` (unique indexed string) stores the bot's secret authentication token (`SecureRandom.base58(24)`), generated on creation when `role == "bot"`.
- `users.webhook_url` (optional string) stores the bot's HTTP webhook callback URL, normalized from blank strings to `nil` so clearing the field removes the webhook. Validated as an HTTP/HTTPS URL with a host (private/loopback hosts are permitted for self-hosted/local bot services).
- `users.add_to_all_open_rooms` (boolean, default `false`, `null: false`) controls whether a bot automatically joins all open rooms. By default bots do not join open rooms automatically (human users still do).
- `users.creator_id` (foreign key to `users`) tracks who created the bot so `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)` naturally grants access to administrators and the bot's creator.
- Modeling bots as `User` records allows bots to reuse:
  - `Membership` (toggle-based assignment on both `Rooms::Open` and `Rooms::Closed`, optional auto-joining on `Rooms::Open`, `@mention` autocomplete, and unread tracking).
  - `Message#creator` (`belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User"`), displaying the bot's name and avatar in messages and web push notifications.
  - `User::Avatar` (`fresh_user_avatar_path`, uploaded avatars, and SVG initials fallback).
- Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate` (sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token`, `webhook_url`, and `add_to_all_open_rooms: false`, removes non-direct room memberships) so historical messages remain intact with the bot's name while immediately revoking API access and webhook delivery.
- Human-only surfaces (`AccountsController`, `Accounts::UsersController`, `SessionsController`, `Sessions::TransfersController`, `Users::BansController`, `Users::SidebarsController`) scope to `User.not_bot` so bots cannot log in, be promoted/banned, or clutter account member lists.

## Open Room Membership Control
- `User.auto_joining_open_rooms` scopes to `not_bot.or(bot.where(add_to_all_open_rooms: true))`.
- `Rooms::Open#grant_access_to_all_users` uses `User.active.auto_joining_open_rooms`, so creating an open room or converting a closed room to open adds all active people and any bots with `add_to_all_open_rooms: true`.
- Turning `add_to_all_open_rooms` on (on creation or update via `after_update_commit`) grants memberships to all existing `Rooms::Open` via `Membership.insert_all(..., returning: %w[ room_id ])`. Turning it off keeps all existing memberships.
- `Rooms::OpensController` and `rooms/opens/_user.html.erb` render checkmarks for people and auto-joining bots, and toggle switches (`user_ids[]`) for bots with `add_to_all_open_rooms: false` so admins/room creators can manually add or remove those bots in individual open rooms.

## HTTP API (Async Posting)
- `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` handled by `Rooms::BotMessagesController#create`.
- Skips session authentication and CSRF forgery protection; authenticates via `User.authenticate_bot(params[:bot_code])` (`active.bot.find_by(bot_token: ...)`).
- Reads `request.raw_post` (forced to UTF-8) directly as the message body so shell scripts/CI jobs can use `curl -d "..."` without JSON envelopes or form-decoding corruption. Supports `multipart/form-data` with `attachment` file uploads via `create_with_attachment!`.
- Broadcasts the message (`@message.broadcast_create`) and triggers `Room::PushMessageJob` via `Message`'s `after_create_commit` callback.

## Outgoing Webhooks (Mentions, Joined & Sync Replies)
- **Mention events**: When a message is committed (`Message` `after_create_commit -> { room.receive(self) }`), `Room#deliver_webhooks_later` enqueues one `Bot::WebhookJob` per mentioned active bot in the room that has a `webhook_url` (excluding the message creator to avoid self-loops).
- **Joined events**: Whenever a bot is newly added to a non-direct room (`Rooms::Open` or `Rooms::Closed`), either automatically (`add_to_all_open_rooms`) or manually (`grant_to` / `Membership.create!`), `Bot::WebhookJob` is enqueued with `(bot, room)` once per newly created membership (after transaction commit). Bulk `Membership.insert_all(..., returning: ...)` guarantees existing memberships do not trigger duplicate `joined` events. `Rooms::Direct` never triggers `joined`.
- `Bot::Webhook` posts `Content-Type: application/json` to `bot.webhook_url` asynchronously in `Bot::WebhookJob`:
  - `mention` payload includes `event`, `author`, `room`, and `message` (stripping only the target bot's mention node from `message.body.text`).
  - `joined` payload includes `event: "joined"` and `room: { id, name, reply_to }`.
- For both events, a `200` response with `Content-Type: text/plain` or `text/html` (and non-blank body) posts a reply message into the room as the bot and calls `broadcast_create`. `204` (or non-200/unsupported content type) posts nothing.

## Per-Member Bot Limit
- `Account` stores `bots_per_member: 5` (default `5`, non-negative integer validated on `Account`) inside `has_json :settings`.
- Administrators can configure `"Bots per member"` on `/account/edit` (`AccountsController#update` renders `:edit` with `422` if invalid).
- `User#bot_limit_reached?` returns `false` for administrators and checks `created_bots.active.count >= Current.account.settings.bots_per_member` for members. Deactivated (deleted) bots do not count toward the limit, and lowering the limit leaves existing bots intact while blocking creation of new ones.
- On `/bots` (`app/views/bots/index.html.erb`), when `Current.user.bot_limit_reached?` is true, the `"Add a chat bot"` link is omitted and a message stating the user has `"reached the limit"` is shown instead.
- `BotsController` enforces `before_action :ensure_within_bot_limit, only: %i[ new create ]` returning `403 Forbidden` to block direct `GET /bots/new` and `POST /bots` attempts at or above the limit.

    suspended_at.present?
  end

  def in_cooldown?(at = Time.current)
    cooldown_until.present? && at < cooldown_until

  def cooldown_seconds_remaining(at = Time.current)
    return 0 unless in_cooldown?(at)

    [ (cooldown_until - at).ceil, 1 ].max
  end

  def attempt_message_post(valid: true)
    with_lock do
      return [ :suspended, nil ] if suspended?

      now = Time.current
      if in_cooldown?(now)
        retry_after = cooldown_seconds_remaining(now)
        record_cooldown_attempt!(now)
        return [ :cooldown, retry_after ]
      end

      return [ :invalid, nil ] unless valid

      timestamps = pruned_post_timestamps(now)
      if timestamps.size >= FLOOD_MESSAGE_LIMIT
        start_cooldown!(now, timestamps)
        return [ :cooldown, FLOOD_COOLDOWN.to_i ]
      end

      message = yield
      if message
        timestamps << time_to_microseconds(now)
        update!(recent_post_timestamps: timestamps, cooldown_until: nil, cooldown_attempts: 0)
        [ :ok, nil ]
      else
        [ :invalid, nil ]
      end
    end

    with_lock do
      return if suspended?

      update!(webhook_failures_count: 0) if webhook_failures_count > 0
    end
  end

  def record_webhook_failure!
    with_lock do
      return if suspended?

      failures = webhook_failures_count + 1
      if failures >= WEBHOOK_FAILURE_LIMIT
        update!(
          webhook_failures_count: failures,
          suspended_at: Time.current,
          suspension_reason: WEBHOOK_SUSPENSION_REASON

      else

      end
    end
  end

      suspension_reason: nil,
      cooldown_until: nil,
      cooldown_attempts: 0,
      webhook_failures_count: 0,

        cooldown_attempts: 0,
        recent_post_timestamps: timestamps
      )
    end

      attempts = cooldown_attempts + 1

        update!(

          suspended_at: now,
          suspension_reason: FLOOD_SUSPENSION_REASON

        update!(cooldown_attempts: attempts)
      end
    end

    limit = Current.account&.settings&.bots_per_member
    !limit.nil? && created_bots.active.count >= limit
  end

  def suspended?
    suspended_at.present?
  end

  def in_cooldown?(at = Time.current)
    cooldown_until.present? && at < cooldown_until
  end

  def cooldown_seconds_remaining(at = Time.current)
    return 0 unless in_cooldown?(at)

    [ (cooldown_until - at).ceil, 1 ].max
  end

  def attempt_message_post(valid: true)
    status, retry_after = with_lock do
      next [ :suspended, nil ] if suspended?

      now = Time.current
      if in_cooldown?(now)
        seconds_left = cooldown_seconds_remaining(now)
        record_cooldown_attempt!(now)
        next [ :cooldown, seconds_left ]
      end

      next [ :invalid, nil ] unless valid

      timestamps = pruned_post_timestamps(now)
      if timestamps.size >= FLOOD_MESSAGE_LIMIT
        start_cooldown!(now, timestamps)
        next [ :cooldown, FLOOD_COOLDOWN.to_i ]
      end

      timestamps << time_to_microseconds(now)
      update!(recent_post_timestamps: timestamps, cooldown_until: nil, cooldown_attempts: 0)
      [ :allowed, nil ]
    end

    return [ status, retry_after ] unless status == :allowed

    yield ? [ :ok, nil ] : [ :invalid, nil ]
  end

  def record_webhook_success!
    with_lock do
      return if suspended?

      update!(webhook_failures_count: 0) if webhook_failures_count > 0
    end
  end

  def record_webhook_failure!
    with_lock do
      return if suspended?

      failures = webhook_failures_count + 1
      if failures >= WEBHOOK_FAILURE_LIMIT
        update!(
          webhook_failures_count: failures,
          suspended_at: Time.current,
          suspension_reason: WEBHOOK_SUSPENSION_REASON
        )
      else
        update!(webhook_failures_count: failures)
      end
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(
      suspended_at: nil,
      suspension_reason: nil,
      cooldown_until: nil,
      cooldown_attempts: 0,
      webhook_failures_count: 0,
      recent_post_timestamps: []
    )
  end

  private
    def pruned_post_timestamps(now)
      cutoff_us = time_to_microseconds(now) - FLOOD_WINDOW_MICROSECONDS
      Array(recent_post_timestamps).select { |ts| ts > cutoff_us }
    end

    def time_to_microseconds(time)
      time.to_i * 1_000_000 + time.usec
    end

    def start_cooldown!(now, timestamps)
      update!(
        cooldown_until: now + FLOOD_COOLDOWN,
        cooldown_attempts: 0,
        recent_post_timestamps: timestamps
      )
    end

    def record_cooldown_attempt!(now)
      attempts = cooldown_attempts + 1
      if attempts >= COOLDOWN_SUSPENSION_ATTEMPTS
        update!(
          cooldown_attempts: attempts,
          suspended_at: now,
          suspension_reason: FLOOD_SUSPENSION_REASON
        )
      else
        update!(cooldown_attempts: attempts)
      end
    end

    def assign_bot_defaults
      self.password_digest ||= ""
      self.bot_token ||= generate_bot_token
    end

    def generate_bot_token
      loop do
        token = SecureRandom.base58(24)
        break token unless User.exists?(bot_token: token)
      end
    end

    def valid_webhook_url
      uri = URI.parse(webhook_url)
      unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?
        errors.add(:webhook_url, "must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL")
      end
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      errors.add(:webhook_url, "must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL")
    end
end

steps.reasoning_content:
**End-to-End Integration Testing Strategy**

Alright, no Chrome or ChromeDriver in this environment – that's expected since we're containerized and have no internet access for downloads. Good thing we thoroughly validated the UI markup with `data: { turbo_confirm: ... }` and our existing integration tests. That was a smart move!

Now, let's craft a robust end-to-end integration test. I think we should place it in `test/controllers/bots_controller_test.rb`, or maybe `test/integration/` might be better. This test needs to comprehensively cover:

1.  **Bot Moderation Workflow:** We'll simulate a bot flood through the API, triggering the cooldown mechanism. The test will need to verify 5 attempts resulting in suspension, a 403 Forbidden response, and the lack of webhooks. It should confirm the bot's status on `/bots` is "Suspended" with the correct reason. Then, we'll simulate an admin clicking Reactivate (via `POST /bots/:id/reactivation`) and confirm the bot can successfully post and receive webhooks again.

2.  **Webhook Failure Scenario:** We need to simulate a bot failing webhooks 10 times, leading to suspension. The test should verify that the bot's status on `/bots` correctly displays as "Suspended" with a reason. Afterward, we'll simulate the admin reactivation and confirm that the bot can once again receive webhooks.

I'll be sure to add this test to `test/controllers/bots_controller_test.rb` (or `test/integration/`), and I'll also update `docs/bots.md` with some solid design notes on the bot moderation system.

\#{mention_attachment_for(@kevin_bot)} ping
", client_message_id: "while-suspended") end # Admin reactivates on bots page sign_in :david post bot_reactivation_url(@kevin_bot) assert_redirected_to bots_url assert_not @kevin_bot.reload.suspended? # Bot can post and receive webhooks again post room_bot_messages_url(room, @kevin_bot.bot_token), params: "Back online" assert_response :created WebMock.stub_request(:post, "https://bot.example.com/webhook").to_return(status: 204, body: "") assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Bot::WebhookJob do room.messages.create!(creator: @david, body: "
\#{mention_attachment_for(@kevin_bot)} welcome back
", client_message_id: "after-reactivate") end perform_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::WebhookJob assert_requested :post, "https://bot.example.com/webhook", times: 1 end end end RUBY src.sub!(/\nend\s*\z/, "\n" + extra) or raise "could not replace end in bots_controller_test.rb" File.write(path, src) ' cat <<'EOF' >> docs/bots.md ## Moderation: Flood Protection, Webhook Failures & Suspension - **Suspension State on `User`**: Suspended bots remain `status: :active` (so they stay listed on `/bots`, retain their rooms/messages, and continue counting toward their owner's `bots_per_member` limit) and track suspension via `suspended_at` and `suspension_reason` (`User::Bot#suspended?`). - **Flooding Limits**: - `User::Bot#attempt_message_post` uses a row lock (`with_lock`) to enforce a sliding 10-second window (`FLOOD_WINDOW_MICROSECONDS = 10_000_000`) stored in `users.recent_post_timestamps` (integer microseconds to avoid float rounding and SQLite `freeze_time` issues). - Both `Rooms::BotMessagesController#create` (API posts) and `Bot::Webhook#handle_response` (webhook `200` replies) share `attempt_message_post`. - Posting an 11th message within 10 seconds rejects the message and starts a 30-second cooldown (`cooldown_until`, `cooldown_attempts = 0`). - During cooldown, `Rooms::BotMessagesController#create` responds with `429 Too Many Requests` and `Retry-After` (integer seconds remaining via `ceil`, minimum `1`), and webhook replies are not posted. - Five more post attempts during the same cooldown suspend the bot (`Flooding: too many messages`). If the cooldown expires with fewer than 5 attempts, the next post clears the cooldown state. - **Webhook Failure Tracking**: - `Bot::Webhook#deliver` wraps only `post_payload` in network/timeout exception handling. Any non-`2xx` response (`!response.is_a?(Net::HTTPSuccess)`), timeout, or connection error calls `bot.record_webhook_failure!`. - Any `2xx` response calls `bot.record_webhook_success!` (resetting `webhook_failures_count` to `0`). - Ten consecutive failed deliveries suspend the bot (`Failing webhooks: 10 consecutive failed deliveries`). - **Suspended Bot Enforcement**: - `Rooms::BotMessagesController` returns `403 Forbidden` via `ensure_not_suspended` (before `set_room`). - `Room#deliver_webhooks_later`, `Room#memberships.grant_to`, `Membership#deliver_joined_webhook_later`, `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms`, and `Bot::Webhook#eligible?` all exclude suspended bots so no webhooks are enqueued or delivered. - **Administrator Reactivation**: - `app/views/bots/_bot.html.erb` renders `"Suspended"` with `suspension_reason` for suspended bots, and renders a `"Reactivate"` button with `data-turbo-confirm` (native browser `confirm()`) only when `Current.user.administrator?`. - `Bots::ReactivationsController#create` (`POST /bots/:bot_id/reactivation`) enforces `Current.user.administrator?` (`403 Forbidden` for non-admins) and calls `@bot.reactivate!`, which clears suspension, cooldown, recent post timestamps, and webhook failure counters. EOF
